public_body: Salem City Council Committee On Ordinances, Licenses & Legal Affairs
overall: The AG found the wetlands working group was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law under the Connelly exception, so neither the Group nor the Committee violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee created a wetlands working group that met on several occasions without complying with the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Group is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law, and neither the Committee nor the Group violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Whether the working group was a public body under the Connelly exception, since an individual official (Senior Planner) assembled it to assist his own responsibilities.
allegations.key_passage: the Group was not subject to the Open Meeting Law, and could not have violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Committee argued the group is not a public body because it is not a body empowered to act collectively.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find the Group was not subject to the Open Meeting Law for this reason, we need not address

allegations.summary: Whether the Committee itself deliberated outside a posted meeting; the complaint focused on the Committee's creation of the group, not its own deliberations.
allegations.key_passage: there are no allegations in the Complaint that the Committee itself engaged in deliberations outside of a posted meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
